text:
maya: Hey team — quick sync on the Autoscale panel mock. Need a few decisions so I can lock the dev tickets. Main points:
1) SLO slider guardrail state: should the guardrail be phrased as 'Recommended limit' (soft) or 'Safety limit' (stronger)?
2) Min/Max inline help copy — short tooltip for what min vs max means for latency vs cost.
3) Burst pill wording — do we show absolute GPUs (+2) or percent (+50%) by default?
4) GPU pool picker keyboard behavior — current prototype traps focus in the dropdown. Accessibility concern.
Mock link: https://figma.redwood/infer/autoscale/panel-2 (see frames B/C).

liam: my vote is 'Recommended limit' — we can still enforce fallback policies, but wording should feel non-alarming for self-serve customers. :+1:

eva: Accessibility: the yellow guardrail stroke on the slider fails contrast on small thumb sizes (AA). We should either darken the stroke or add a 1px dashed outline for focus. Also keyboard trap is a showstopper — picker must allow arrow key nav + escape to close.

jordan: copy suggestions — keeping it minimal. Proposed microcopy block below (feel free to tweak):

```
Min: Guaranteed resources to keep latency within target during steady load.
Max: Upper bound we can scale to during bursts; may increase cost.
Guardrail (recommended): Keeps your latency under SLO most of the time; we may throttle bursts that exceed this.
Burst pill: "+2 GPUs (temp)"  — shows absolute by default, with hover showing +50%
```

maya: I like showing absolute GPUs first (easier to parse), hover reveals percent. For very large pools percent is more meaningful though — maybe switch label based on pool size (if pool >=8 GPUs show percent).

liam: Agree on adaptive label. Also: can we add an inline 'why this matters' link next to the slider that opens a tiny tooltip with a two-line explainer? Helps reduce cognitive load.

eva: +1 to tooltip. Also request: add aria-live updates when the slider value changes so screen reader users hear new min/max values and any guardrail warnings.

maya: Good call. For the keyboard trap, current behavior captures focus because we render virtualized pool items. Jordan — can we change to roving tabindex pattern so arrow keys move focus but Escape/Tab still leave the menu?

jordan: Yes — will update prototype to use roving tabindex and ensure Escape returns focus to the pool selector button. I'll also increase guardrail stroke to #B36A00 to pass AA on 14px.

qa-bot: Created ticket INF-3129: autoscale-accessibility-keyboard. Steps to repro, prioritized P1. (link: https://tracker.redwood/INF-3129)

liam: microcopy nit — in the guardrail line 'we may throttle bursts that exceed this' sounds punitive. Maybe: 'requests beyond this may route to a lower-priority pool' — more precise.

jordan: Good wording. New guardrail line: 'Requests beyond this may be routed to lower-priority capacity.'

maya: OK I'm updating the mock and will post a follow-up with updated frames and a small A/B copy test for guardrail phrasing. Thanks all — will tag eng after mock updates. :sparkles:

eva: Thanks — will validate contrast changes and screen reader flow once new prototype is up.

liam: one last ask — add a subtle keyboard hint under the pool picker: 'Use ↑ ↓ to preview pools, Enter to select, Esc to close'. Small text, but helpful for power users.

maya: added to TODO. Closing for now, will reopen thread with new frames later.
